claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy is single-phase BCC.
The initial TiVNbTa alloy has a dendritic microstructure.
The initial TiVNbTa alloy contains no secondary-phase dispersion.
The baseline TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of about 330 MPa at 1273 K under testing involving 30% strain.
Reactive synthesis or powder metallurgy followed by heat treatment can establish a uniform nanoscale Y2O3 dispersion in TiVNbTa.
The intervention produces nanoscale Y2O3 particles distributed within the BCC TiVNbTa matrix.
Dispersed Y2O3 particles retard dislocation motion at elevated temperature.
Dispersed Y2O3 particles inhibit grain-boundary sliding at elevated temperature.
Retarding dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding delays plastic deformation and preserves yield strength at 1273 K.
Oxide-dispersion-strengthened TiVNbTa will have a yield strength of approximately 400–450 MPa at 1273 K.
Oxide-dispersion-strengthened TiVNbTa will have improved mechanical stability during high-temperature testing relative to the baseline alloy.
The proposed intervention is applicable at temperatures up to 1273 K.
The proposed intervention is applicable under tensile and compressive loading involving strains of about 30–40%.
A controlled comparison should use otherwise equivalent TiVNbTa samples with and without oxide particles under identical thermal and mechanical test regimes.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant yield-strength increase above approximately 330 MPa at 1273 K, together with failure to improve mechanical stability, would falsify the hypothesis.
